posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
With floor autotiles, each 96x144 section of the tilesheet shows as one tile in the editor. The editor palette just shows the top left portion of the tile, but the whole thing is used when you actually put that tile on a map.
I think you may have put the autotiles you're working with on the wrong sheet – they are A2 tiles, not A1 tiles. That is, when you edit the tileset in the database, you should put the tilesheet you just made into the A2 slot of that tileset, and not the A1 slot or any other slot.
There are actually 4 different types of autotiles in RPGMaker, each with their own specifications. You can see the help file (press F1 in the editor) for details on all the different autotiles, but I'll summarize the basics for you here:
Animated autotiles are placed on the A1 tilesheet. They consist of 3 96x144 blocks like the one you've shown, and the game cycles between the 3 versions.
Waterfall autotiles are also placed on the A1 tilesheet. They consist of 3 96x48 blocks, which the game cycles between. The 3 blocks combine into a 96x144 block.
Floor autotiles are mostly placed on the A2 tilesheet, but there's also space for two of them on the A1 sheet, and wall top tiles on A4 also follow the same specification. This is the format you've shown in this thread.
Wall/roof autotiles go on the A3 and A4 tilesheets. These are a 96x96 block. On A3, the top and side are both in the wall/roof format, while on A4, the side uses the wall/roof format while the top uses the same format as floor autotiles.
All other tiles (which can go on A5, B, C, D, or E) are 48x48 tiles with no automatic functions.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
The tiles you showed are clearly intended to be autotiles (they fit perfectly into the specification of how autotiles work). So placing each of the 6 tiles there individually just isn't a thing. What the game engine actually does with that 96x144 block is to cut it up into 24x24 tiles, which it remixes to produce a total of 47 different possible 48x48 tiles. You can use copy-paste (right-click) and shift-click to put a specific one of those 47 tiles in an arbitrary place, but you can't paint them like that directly from the terrain palette.
If you have other tiles that
aren't
meant to be tiles, the sheets must be placed in the A5 slot or one of the non-A slots (B through E). Those tiles need to be 48x48 each.
I'm not quite sure how you got the particular editor screenshot you showed, as the sample you posted, as presented, would not have shown up like that in the editor. If you want specific help, you'll need to show the exact asset placed in the tilesets folder. It
may
also help to show a screenshot of the tileset in the database.
